subject.title: fix(gateway): enforce plugin-ownership check in sessions.patch

question: Is the existing `sessions.delete` rule sufficient precedent to reject every plugin-runtime patch of a legacy ownerless row, or must OpenClaw provide a doctor/operator migration or recovery path before enforcing that rule?
rationale: The strict rule closes cross-plugin adoption and mutation, but it deliberately makes a persisted workflow that previously succeeded fail closed; repository policy requires explicit owner judgment for that security-versus-upgrade boundary.

options.title: Approve strict fence
options.body: Treat ownerless rows as having no plugin authority, retain fail-closed rejection, and require proof that an operator or non-plugin client can recover them.

options.title: Require migration path
options.body: Add an explicit doctor or operator-owned migration that assigns safe ownership before plugin-runtime patch access is denied.

recommendation.title: Approve strict fence
recommendation.body: Treat ownerless rows as having no plugin authority, retain fail-closed rejection, and require proof that an operator or non-plugin client can recover them.

likelyOwner.reason: This decision crosses Gateway security, persisted session compatibility, and product upgrade policy rather than being only a local implementation choice.
